columns.event_key: Awaiting You (S1, TASK-1371): dotted domain key (e.g. artwork.proof_uploaded) the relay matches rules against. `type` stays the display enum.

notes.model: A registered PLX agent. `slug` is the stable public identifier used by `/api/agents/<slug>/*` and as the knowledge namespace.

columns.active_version_id: Pointer to the version invocations resolve against. Set after v1 exists.

notes.model: An invocation grant, expressed on the portal's two orthogonal authorization axes (see lib/auth/roles.ts and lib/auth/department-roles.ts): minRole         — authority floor, hierarchical. "STAFF" also covers MANAGER, ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN, matching requireRole(). departmentScope — functional scope, set-valued. Empty means every department. The axes are deliberately NOT merged into composite roles such as "QC-MANAGER": that is a cartesian product growing with every department, and it destroys the hierarchy the rest of the portal depends on. A grant never widens power: effective action power is always the agent's capability set intersected with the caller's own RBAC.

Append-only control-plane audit: configuration mutations from the Admin API and, once the thin adapter lands, invocation decisions (CHAT_TURN / PERMISSION_DENIED). `action` is a string so new actions need no migration.

columns.metadata: Never store message content or secrets here.

notes.model: One case of an agent eval suite (agent fleet P15a, D25). `input` is what the agent gets; `checks` holds the deterministic assertions plus an optional rubric for the judge model. A changed `updatedAt` marks the case as changed, so a cached result for it no longer counts (P15).

The result of one case in one eval run (agent fleet P15a, D25). `versionId` is the version the case ran as: the candidate, or the baseline when the run had no cached baseline result to reuse (P15). Its foreign key cascades, so deleting an agent removes its versions and results in one statement; a version with eval runs still cannot be deleted on its own.

columns.score: Judge score, when the case has a rubric.
columns.judge_model: Fleet alias of the judge model, when a judge scored the case.
columns.transcript_ref: Where the run's transcript for this case is stored.

notes.model: One eval of a candidate agent version against a baseline, normally the active version (agent fleet P15a, D25). The runner claims it, heartbeats and polls like any run (P15, SC-4), so P4's stale sweep covers it.

columns.baseline_version_id: The version the candidate is compared with. Null when the agent had no active version at enqueue. The gate refuses a run whose baseline is no longer the active version (P15).
columns.suite: The suite id from the candidate's `evalConfig.suite`.
columns.pass_rate: Share of cases passed, 0 to 1. Set when the run ends.
columns.usd: Spend in US dollars, read from the run's eval key (P2, P15).
columns.claimed_by: The runner that claimed the run.

notes.model: Pause state of one agent loop (agent fleet P4a). The run-end rule pauses a loop, never the agent; only an ADMIN clears the pause. The runner API (P4) also locks this row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) while it counts RUNNING runs.
Append-only transcript row mirrored from the runtime engine.

columns.seq: Mirrors TripleTMessage.seq so ordering is stable when two rows share a createdAt. Nullable because a non-mirrored message may not carry one.
columns.metadata: toolCalls, routingDecision, evalScores — null until the engine emits them.

notes.model: One run of one agent loop on the fleet runner (agent fleet P4a, D19). It follows the portal's job-run pattern (caller, correlation id, mode, lock), like `WorkRoutingRun`, in its own table because that one does not fit. The runner API (P4) writes it; the runner never sets its own approval state.

columns.version_id: The agent version the run executes.
columns.caller: Who started the run. Only `runner` today (D19).
columns.usd: Spend in US dollars, read from the run's own fleet proxy key (P4).
columns.approved_version_id: The agent version the ADMIN approved.
columns.uat_run_id: The `UatAgentRun` a `uat-job` run serves. Unique: the runner gets at most one claim per `UatAgentRun`; a retry after a runner failure goes to Cursor.

notes.model: Registry-side conversation. During the transition it MIRRORS the runtime-native conversation (`externalConversationId` = TripleTConversation.id) rather than replacing it, so existing /api/triple-t/* clients keep working.

columns.agent_version_id: Version resolved when the thread was opened, for reproducibility.
columns.status: ACTIVE | FINALIZED | ARCHIVED — the adapter rejects terminal threads.
columns.metadata: Non-secret routing/observability context. Never store credentials.

notes.model: One revision of an agent definition. Append-only: a configuration change is always a new row, never an edit, so what an agent was configured to do at invocation time stays reproducible. Each capability is its own nullable column. A new capability type is an additive nullable column and older rows read null, so the contract can grow without invalidating already-published versions.

columns.persona: Declarative system-prompt intent. Recorded for Admin and a future controlled override; phase 1 still runs the hardcoded Tristan prompt.
columns.mcp_allow_list: MCP servers this agent may reach, e.g. ["plx-uat-solver"]. Empty denies every MCP, mirroring `isTripleTMcpEnabled() === false`.

notes.model: TASK-1364 gap 6: AO label reconciliation (SOP form #013B). One row per label stock issued to the AO; received must equal used + rejected + returned.

columns.ao_id: bronze public.assembly_order.id (no FK — bronze is FM-synced).
columns.ao_number: Display copy; the AO code can be renumbered.

notes.model: Append-only QA sign-off of an AO's label reconciliation (#013B).
Append-only in-process line inspection (#010). AQL 1%: Ac 0 / Re 1.
Append-only: a QC release made with open gaps, acknowledged with a reason (ERP-D-029 warn-only; SOP QC-005 §5.2.5(b)).

TASK-1350: floor-actuals sidecar keyed to the bronze `public.production` task (no FK — bronze is FM-synced). Downtime minutes + coded reason (code-side vocabulary, plain text column) + comment. `projectKey` / `routingVersion` are denormalised at write time from the AO's AoSetupSnapshot so a later routing revision cannot rewrite history.

columns.ao_id: bronze public.assembly_order.id (no FK — bronze is FM-synced).
columns.production_task_id: bronze public.production.id; partial unique in SQL (WHERE NOT NULL).

notes.model: Persisted standard routing for an FG (project key). Quote, schedule, AO print, and efficiency all read this row instead of re-deriving or faking 1-hour labour. Unrouted FGs are reported, never silently defaulted. ARCH-06 A6-D5 — the setup sheet snapshotted onto every AO at creation (permanent ERP-grade pattern). `payload` holds labels, QC, case & pallet, line, instructions, routing standards (setup/changeover minutes, crew, bpm), and the pallet-drawing ref. The printed assembly card prefers this row; live join is only a labeled fallback for pre-snapshot AOs. Shape: `lib/final-products/ao-setup-snapshot.ts`. Re-snapshot is an explicit, audited STAFF action (stamps resnapshotted_at / resnapshot_by_id).

columns.ao_id: bronze public.assembly_order.id (no FK — bronze is FM-synced).

notes.model: Admin-issued API credentials for external/third-party API access (/api/external/*). The raw key (`plx_<48 hex>`) is shown ONCE at creation; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Managed at /admin/api-keys, verified by lib/auth/api-keys.ts. Revocation is soft (revokedAt) for audit history. `scopes` says what a key opens: `external` opens /api/external/*. The migration 20260929200000_api_key_scopes gave every earlier key `external`. The default stays `external`: an insert that names no scopes (the code before P12a) makes an external key. Every newer writer sets `scopes` itself.

P4 staging-only test receiving. A portal-owned test lot that staff can receive, QC, release and pick for a batch on staging. It is never FileMaker data: the table is not in fm_staging_sync.py SYNC_TABLES and has no FK or view on any FM-mirror table, so the sync never touches it. Production never reads it (isTestReceivingEnabled keeps the SQL out). Lot numbers and lab IDs carry the TEST- prefix. CHECK constraints on origin and status live in the migration.

P4: one row per batch line that uses a test lot. batch_id and batch_item_id point at the FM-mirror public.batch / batch_item tables with NO FK on purpose. batch_fingerprint (namebatch_c + creation time) lets the purge tell our test batch from a FileMaker batch that later reused the same id. released_at frees the qty (cancel, line change, purge).

TASK-2742: immutable formula/IL check basis for an artwork attachment version. Plain text identifiers have no relations. Only supersededAt and stale* may change. The current-basis formulationId index (WHERE superseded_at IS NULL) lives in migration SQL.
TASK-2629: append-only exact proof-version decisions; QA acceptance remains separate.

TASK-2626 (ERP-D-019): an artwork version (an `app_attachment` proof) that got its own P- packaging item. Written only by lib/artwork/artwork-version-switch.ts. One item per version; the FG keeps its FG-xxxx and its Pack BOM moves to a new version that lines the new item.

notes.model: One gold sourcing family for legacy raw-material requests and packaging requests created from a theoretical Assembly BOM line (MRP-M-143).
Physical packaging samples sent by a vendor for one sourcing request. A request can link only after at least one sample reaches ACCEPTED.

One outbound message to a Supplier that carries two or more packaging sourcing requests. Each request keeps its own response, drawing, sample, and Product-link gates; the package has no bulk-link action.
Membership of one sourcing request in one vendor package. Request-level workflow state remains the source of truth for every line gate.

Records the resolved SharePoint site/drive/ item so the file can be queried/downloaded from the right location even if the storage config later changes. Soft-deleted (deletedAt) for audit.

Written only by lib/artwork/decide-proof.ts (set on APPROVED, cleared on any other decision); read by the pack-proof store and frozen onto the FG revision. columns.retention_label: TASK-2250: retention label the worker applied and read back; null when no label is configured for the category.

notes.model: Read model of BC sales credit memos (AR credits). Separate from bc_invoice_snapshot, which has no document type (TASK-803).

Private staff scratchpad item (My Bench). Always owner-scoped — list/get/ mutate paths must filter on ownerUserId. File bytes live on Attachment with entityType=BENCH_ITEM; note body lives here. Never auto-delete.

columns.customer_ref: The unified /mrp customer key (FM bronze id or app_customer_local cuid).

columns.submission: The brief submission returned through this invite (lib/leads/schema.ts).

Confidential capabilities / pitch deck record for a Customer (optional Project link).

Per-draft FG / projectKey copy + override of a template cost matrix row. Seed path copies matrix values here (`source=seed`). Later edits stay on this row (`draft` / `confirmed`) and never mutate the template tables.

columns.overhead_per_unit: Assembly-only. Compounding rows leave this null.

A mailbox the portal may send from. Must also be in the Exchange scope group.
Editable routing for one email type. Keys are declared in code (lib/email-hub/catalog.ts).

Rows are never edited; a change writes a new version and demotes the old one (`isActive` is the only column that changes).

columns.action_keys: Selected line-action keys (touches). Empty array when authored from a diagram snapshot.
columns.standard_hours_per_unit: operators ÷ (bpm × 60). Null when bpm is missing — never invent 1 hour.

Dual-key idiom exactly like StabilityStudy (R6): portal linkage via `formulationId` (gold app_formulation.id), FM linkage via `fmFormulaId` (bronze public.formula.id; the gold projection's external_id is "fm-form-{id}"). columns.fm_formula_id: Bronze public.formula.id (FM). Nullable; app-level writes always stamp at least one of the two keys.

columns.confirmed_at: R&D confirmation stamp (STAFF). NULL = unconfirmed → reported-missing.

notes.model: Per-field audit log for PLX edits to bronze public.formula_item rows. FM-originated changes via fm_staging_sync.py are NOT recorded here. See docs/modules/formulations/README.md.

Lookup of canonical R&D formula progress values. See migration scripts/migrations/20260512_create_app_formula_progress_options.sql.

Per-ingredient actual quantity + lot number captured by R&D when a formula sample is weighed in the lab. Header sample fields (size, dates, QC test parameters) live on bronze public.formula directly. This gold table only captures what R&D entered by hand on each sample run — kept separate so bronze public.formula_item is never extended with portal- only columns. One row per (formulaId, formulaItemId) — upserted on save. See portal/src/app/api/mrp/formulas/[id]/sample/route.ts.

The case-insensitive unique (formula_id, lower(label)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL lives only in the migration SQL (Prisma cannot express it). See portal/src/app/api/mrp/formulas/[id]/spec-rows/route.ts.

TASK-2627: Form #012, incoming QC of a packaging receipt line (SOP QC-003). Snapshots the customer-approved artwork version as the standard the pack is checked against, computes the MIL-STD-105E S-4 sample size from the lot size and logs the retained sample. PASS lets the receipt release; FAIL opens an NCR (an app_deviation row, deviationId). Attachment and deviation ids are plain ids with no FK.

columns.supply_source: G-D10 lot-level marker: 'CUSTOMER_SUPPLIED' on lots of a CUSTOMER_SUPPLIED receipt (customer-owned at $0, not 3PL billable); NULL on every other lot (TASK-2564).

notes.model: Append-only check of a label layout or content change before its first print. The checker may be the person who made the change. A second person is allowed and is not required. Who checked it is the row.

W5a / OD-16 — Lead: an unverified inbound identity living ONLY in the lead inbox (/mrp/leads). A lead can hold nothing — no projects, briefs, quotes, samples, or portal account; spam dies here. The AM verify action promotes lead → Prospect via the Wave-4 one-motion (customer status Prospect + project + attached brief in one flow); the lead row then just records the promotion (verified_customer_ref / verified_project_key) for audit.

columns.brief: Raw public "Start your project" submission (category, description, benchmarks, target market, volumes chip, target retail/cost, launch timing, pack preference). Shape: lib/leads/schema.ts.
columns.verified_by_user_id: Stamped by the one-motion verify claim: who verified, when, and what was minted (unified /mrp customer key + DR-1 project key).

notes.model: Setup / changeover minutes keyed by line × group × action. lineNumber 0 / groupCode "*" / actionKey "*" are plant-wide wildcards.

columns.action_key: Line-action key, or "*" for group/line-wide default.

notes.model: OH V1 overhead rate store (TASK-2853, Pack BOM v3 handoff O1): the plant overhead rate R, $ CAD per charged line-hour, indirect overhead only (never crew). Not on RateSettings, which is one row with no history. Append-only (a contract on the writer; no trigger enforces it): every save INSERTs a row, a same-day correction included; nothing UPDATEs or DELETEs one. So there is deliberately NO unique key on (lineNumber, effectiveFrom). Resolution for a line at a pricing date: (lineNumber, latest effectiveFrom <= date, latest createdAt), then line 0, then missing. No shift column: a second shift carries the same rate. SQL-only CHECKs (migration 20261014121000_task_2853_line_overhead_rate): line_number >= 0; rate_per_line_hour finite and > 0; inputs is a JSON object; created_by_id and created_by_email not blank. Nothing reads or writes this table yet: the store helpers and the /mrp/overhead-rates admin page follow in their own PRs.

columns.line_number: 0 = plant default (V1 writes only line 0). No line master: lines are integers.
columns.rate_per_line_hour: R. Deliberately no `overheadPer*` prefix: lib/costing/rate-masters.ts reads any key with that prefix as the per-operator-hour rate.
columns.inputs: Immutable sizing snapshot at save: period, budget, pool note, working days and their source, each line's shifts and utilization, 7.5 h, normal hours, suggested R, entered R, look-back figures with their source.
columns.override_note: Required by the writer when R differs from the suggested R by more than 5 %.
columns.created_by_id: Bare actor stamps (no relation), as on LineActionSetupStandard.

notes.model: Fixed list of relationship kinds. Adding a kind is a one-row INSERT, not a schema change. All eight are directed (from → to).
ERP-D-026 / ERP-D-027: one material/document/requirement assertion. A document proving several requirements has one row for each catalog key.

columns.expires_at: Null means never expires. Readers warn at 30 days and flag expired evidence.

notes.model: Per-customer or per-supplier switch and extra copies for one email type. Exactly one party column is set (SQL CHECK).

They join this model with the first code that reads them (S2c, TASK-2683), not before: the verdict upsert returns every model column, so listing them ahead of the migration would fail that route on an unmigrated database (expand-contract).

columns.fm_project_id: Bare public.project.id as text OR app_project_local.id; never fm-proj-<id>. No FK (spans two sources), as in S2a.

columns.sample_dispatch_id: DEV-02: the outbound SampleDispatch (app_sample_dispatch.id) this verdict answers — stamped from the FormRequest row at F4/F6 submit. Joins verdicts to dispatches on the unified /mrp/samples history. No FK by design (loose text ref, same idiom as the dispatch's own bronze refs).
columns.shipping_facts: DEV-02: F4 shipping facts retained from the form instead of discarded — JSON { carrier, trackingNumber, dateShipped, dateReceived, batchNumber, sampleNumber } (all nullable strings; dates ISO). Shape built by projectFeedbackFromForm (lib/project-development/feedback.ts).

notes.model: Project requirement profile (TASK-2681, ERP-D-024/025): the customer requirements a project carries, one row per (project, domain, key), keyed by the bare PD project key, as on ProjectSeedProvenance (never the gold `fm-proj-<id>` stamp). `origin` = 'CUSTOMER' (copied from `sourceRequirementId`, required) | 'PROJECT' (added on the project). `status` = 'ACTIVE' | 'WAIVED' | 'NOT_APPLICABLE' | 'REMOVED'; a removed row stays so the trail and re-seed see it. A PROJECT origin or any status other than ACTIVE needs reason, decidedById and decidedAt. All enforced by DB CHECKs. A changed copied value is stamped on ProjectSeedProvenance.

columns.fm_project_id: Bare PD project key (FM id as text, or the local cuid).
columns.source_requirement_id: The app_customer_requirement row it was copied from (no FK, as on ProjectSeedProvenance — the provenance survives a deleted requirement).

notes.model: CR-D3 copy-at-birth provenance: one row per seeded (project, target). `target` = 'field:<projectEditSchema key>' (e.g. 'field:moq') or 'artwork:<market>:<item>' (e.g. 'artwork:US:GTIN / EAN'). CR-D4 override stamps overriddenAt/overriddenById/overrideReason (reason required; also activity-logged as an ActivityEvent).

columns.requirement_id: The app_customer_requirement row that supplied the value (no FK — the requirement may be deleted later; provenance survives).

notes.model: MRP-M-222 — one calibration snapshot of /mrp/projected-revenue. Cron writes weekly (Monday 07:00 UTC), STAFF can also write on demand. The ribbon overlays each row against Sage OE shipment EXTINVMISC for the same window to render a projection-vs-actual hit-rate %.
STAFF-only Pulse campaign. Seeded campaign ids are stable slugs so Outlook deep links (`/uat/pulse/<campaignId>`) stay durable.
One structured response per staff member per campaign. Scores and opinions stay here. Bug-shaped free text may escalate to canonical Feedback / CoS Seal.
Reusable Staff Pulse question set (score + free text). Seeded in 20260909201500_staff_pulse_mvp. Not Microsoft Forms.

Q2-B (QD-1 LOCKED): the customer's ASKED volumes are the pricing bases — per-quote, first-class. One row per asked volume; the engine renders one volume-matrix column per row. The 5k/10k/25k/50k run-volume ladder is DEMOTED to suggestion chips (RateSettings.quoteSuggestionVolumes) + the seeded standard-cost fallback index — nothing about a quote is band-shaped.

columns.asked_units: Asked run quantity in finished units — THE pricing basis (QD-1).
columns.vessel_code_override: QD-3 estimator override of the deterministic vessel derivation for this asked volume. NULL = derived pick stands. Validated by the engine against the formula's compatibility set; provenance-flagged, never silent.

columns.overhead_per_production_hour: Hourly OH rate ($/operator-hour). W2c / OD-14: the quote engine absorbs this over ASSEMBLY up-time hours only (OH $/unit = rate × up-time ÷ expected units in the shift); compounding/batching carries zero OH.
columns.margin_percent: W2c / OD-13: system default-selected tier of the margin ladder (margin-on-price %; price = cost ÷ (1 − m)).
columns.margin_tiers_pct: W2c / OD-13: governed margin tier ladder (percent, margin-on-price), editable at /mrp/employee-rates. Per-quote overrides live in Quote.customFields and never mutate this row.
columns.sample_cap_dev_units: OD-15 sample-dispatch quantity caps, per class (owner-set 2026-08-24: dev 25 / production 500), editable at /mrp/employee-rates. Production covers ANSI-style AQL sampling sizes on large lots; dev stays tight so a "sample" can never be a stealth order.
columns.quote_suggestion_volumes: Q2-B / OD-Q2: governed asked-volume suggestion chips for new quotes, editable at /mrp/employee-rates. Seeded from the DEMOTED 5k/10k/25k/50k run-volume ladder (QD-1: the customer's asked volumes are the pricing bases; these are only suggestions + the engine's default when a quote has no volumes stored).

notes.model: First-class record links. Each row: from (type + id), to (type + id), kind, who, when, source. A file (attachment) sits at either end. Wrong links are ended (endedAt set) and replaced so the trail keeps its history. Active uniqueness (one link per from/to/kind while endedAt IS NULL) is enforced by a partial unique index in the migration — not a Prisma @@unique.

One entry per portal record kind. Seeded from record-map-data.ts portal nodes plus "attachment" as a file endpoint. Code is the stable identifier; label and page may change without breaking link rows.
Shared run-volume parent for compounding + assembly standard-cost sheets. Codes are plant run sizes (5k / 10k / 25k / 50k), not vendor MOQ breaks.

Portal-raised customer return (TASK-803 / ERP-M-041). Idempotency + audit for the DRAFT-only BC sales credit memo; BC alone posts it. Written by lib/business-central/sales-return.ts. status: DRAFT | SENT | POSTED | FAILED.

W4-S / OD-15 — sample dispatch: the narrow door for samples. Mandatory traceability record for every sample leaving the building; surfaces in the warehouse ready-to-ship queue and flags in lot traceability. Never touches the commercial gate stack (no sales order / ship release / dock scan). `class` is derived from `sampleType` in code (lib/samples/dispatch.ts) — never user-chosen independently. Class B rows are hard-blocked until the bronze source's statusqc is Released (checked at create AND at dispatch).

columns.sample_type: formulation | packaging | draft_fg | bulk_from_batch | in_process_ao | fg_from_ao
columns.project_key: Class A anchor (DR-1 project key). Nullable for Class B.
columns.fm_batch_id: Class B source refs — bronze FM keys as text; no FK into bronze.
columns.qc_signoff_user_id: In-process AO rule: QC's sign-off (user + timestamp) on the dispatch row.

columns.qty_shipped: Recomputed on shipment SHIPPED/CANCELLED — quantity shipped against this release line. Kept denormalized so the dashboard can filter without joins.

columns.fm_formula_id: FM formula the study schedules testing for (bronze public.formula.id). Nullable at the DB level for safety; REQUIRED at the app level for new studies (PD prune R6, D-B: Zod rejects creation without it) — the study is the SCHEDULE, evidence lives on the formula's Documents tab.

notes.model: TASK-2250: durable finalize queue for one uploaded attachment, modelled on WorkRoutingOutbox (dedupe key, attempts, lease, next attempt). The worker writes metadata, applies the retention label, reads both back with the quickXorHash, and sets the attachment READY (or FAILED at maxAttempts).

columns.attachment_id: Exactly one of attachmentId and documentId is set (CHECK app_storage_finalize_job_one_owner_check, TASK-3157).
columns.document_id: TASK-3157: a customer Document's job, one per stored copy.
columns.copy: "customer" | "internal" on a document job, null on an attachment job (CHECK app_storage_finalize_job_copy_check).
columns.dedupe_key: `ATTACHMENT_FINALIZE:<driveId>:<itemId>`: one job per SharePoint item. A document's working copy that has not been stored yet waits under `DOCUMENT_WORKING_COPY:<documentId>` until the worker stores and pins it.
columns.drive_id: TASK-2352: the drive this job finalizes, pinned at enqueue. Null means the default drive (SHAREPOINT_DRIVE_ID).
columns.sharepoint_item_id: TASK-2352: the SharePoint item this job finalizes, pinned at enqueue. The worker reads and writes only this item, never the attachment's current pointer. A null here is read from `dedupeKey` (finalize-queue.ts `pinnedTarget`); a key that does not parse leaves the job unpinned.
columns.metadata: SharePoint column values to write, built at upload time.

notes.model: Admin-editable map of document category → where files are stored. `folderTemplate` supports tokens {customer} {customerCode} {project} {year} {category}. `siteId`/`driveId` are optional per-category overrides (null = use the default SHAREPOINT_SITE_ID / SHAREPOINT_DRIVE_ID), so a category like COA can later be pointed at a different team's SharePoint site without code changes. Read by lib/storage/locations.ts (falls back to a code default map if a row is missing, so uploads never break).
Process 2 (assembly) simplified labour / line / setup / OH matrix per template × tier. Assembly costs are tier-volatile (D6). OH is assembly-only.

columns.rate_bpm: Throughput (units/min). Not a vendor unit-cost rate.

notes.model: Process 1 (bulk / compounding) simplified labour matrix per template × tier. Labour/unit = compounderCount × hours / yieldUnits (locked 2 × 8 / yield). Overhead is assembly-only — this table has no OH column.

columns.source: Catalog rows are `seed`. Changing a template is a separate explicit act.

columns.freshness_checked_at: When the last live freshness check ran.
columns.freshness_live_hash: The live structural hash that check computed. NULL = a priced input could not be read, so the check could not certify fresh.
columns.freshness_engine_version: COSTING_ENGINE_VERSION of the engine that ran the check (the version the live hash is in). A different current version = the engine changed since.
columns.freshness_met: The check's `cost_fresh` verdict: true = met, false = stale.
columns.freshness_reasons: JSON string array of value-named reasons, e.g. ["bom_line (Pump qty 1 → 2)"]; [] when met.

notes.model: Historical Sage / supporting-doc activity for parity months (Phase 1 bridge).

columns.invoice_ref: Phase 2: BC / ERP invoice id once auto-posted

notes.model: Reusable rate-card group (e.g. Dandylion 2025–2026). Customers point at a card.

columns.category: INBOUND | OUTBOUND | STORAGE | HOLDING | SERVICE | MONTHLY
columns.enabled: Per-line toggle: false = fee waived on this card (returned as 0 by rateByCode). Every 3PL contract negotiates line-item exceptions; toggling avoids cloning the whole card just to zero out one row.

notes.model: One authenticated Tristan conversation. Holds the evidence draft assembled through leading questions; on finalize it maps to `commitCanonicalIntake` and links to the created `Feedback` ticket (`feedbackId`, 1:1).

columns.channel: Origin channel stamped onto the resulting intake (fixed for Tristan).
columns.feedback_id: Set once finalized; unique so a conversation maps to at most one ticket.
columns.complexity: Complexity label assigned by Tristan (used later by the model router).

notes.model: Append-only chat transcript for a Tristan conversation.

KPI-derived model/prompt priors for the Triple T coding-model router (P7). Additive gold table. The optimizer aggregates resolved UatAgentRun outcomes (Verified / Failed Retest, attempts, time-to-ready, selectedModel, promptVersion) and writes a versioned prior blob here. `payload` is a self-describing JSON snapshot (model success weights + optional prompt pin); storing it as a blob keeps migrations additive as the scoring shape evolves. Exactly one row per `scope` is `active`; the router reads it via the optimizer helpers (never overriding hard policy: escalation, Critical unlock, or operator kill switches / pins).

columns.scope: Reserved for future segmentation (e.g. per complexity band). "global" today.
columns.prior_version: Monotonic version per scope; the active row carries the latest applied set.
columns.payload: Versioned prior snapshot: { version, modelWeights, promptPin, sampleSize, computedAt }.
columns.metrics_window: Aggregation window + config used to compute this set (provenance).
columns.sample_size: Number of resolved runs backing this prior set.
columns.active: Only the active row is consulted by the router. At most one active per scope.

notes.model: Append-only automation audit events for a run.
Immutable intent outbox with lease/retry metadata for at-least-once relay.
One automation attempt for a Feedback ticket. Never reused across user-test attempts.
Structured clarification questions, drafts, final answers, and resume metadata.
Append-only retest / status history for SharePoint UAT Feedback list items. Keyed by SharePoint list item id (not Postgres app_feedback.id).
Idempotent notification delivery record (Graph mail / in-app).
Hashed, expiring, one-time public clarification response token (raw token never stored).
Durable sliding-window rate-limit events (public submission / clarification). Cleanup deletes rows older than 2× window; fail-closed on DB errors.
Durable webhook delivery-id reservation for invoke HMAC replay protection. Reserved only after a valid signature; expires for cleanup.

columns.location_type: MANUFACTURING | STORAGE | THIRD_PARTY | OTHER — physical site role (not bin/zone).
columns.exclude_from_valuation: 3PL / consignment site: stock here is customer-owned and excluded from PLX inventory valuation / COGS (posts to BC at $0 cost). ERP-M-037.

notes.model: Sage I/C Transfer–aligned warehouse transfer document (MRP-M-059). docType mirrors Sage doctype: TRANSFER(1) / TRANSIT_TRANSFER(2) / TRANSIT_RECEIPT(3).

One unit of routed work for one target (department or named assignee) on one record, from one source system. `openKey` = `dedupeKey` while open, null when closed, so at most one open item per key while history is kept.

columns.department_id: Target department; kept while UNROUTED. Null only for named-actor rules.
columns.assignee_id: Named-actor target (requester's pick, PO approver, mapped BC approver). Distinct from claimedById.

notes.model: External approver identity → portal user (BC User ID per company). Refreshed by S8.

Transactional outbox for work routing. Shape copied from UatAgentOutbox so lease and retry code can be shared. Written in the same transaction as the ActivityEvent by recordActivityEvent, and by the relay for deliveries.
One row per execution of any caller (cron, cli, gha, admin). The health card reads it.
Explicit non-working days (plant holidays). Weekends are implicit in buildLabourDayWindows and do not need rows. Kind HOLIDAY and NON_WORKING both drop the day from labour windows.
